description:
Women’s Summer 2027
by Anthony Vaccarello

“A light shines all the more brightly because we know it cannot be held. What passes sometimes leaves more light than what remains.” Anthony Vaccarello

For Summer 2027, Anthony Vaccarello explores the transformative power of gold, a color deeply rooted in the history of Saint Laurent and beloved by Monsieur Saint Laurent himself.

From sahariennes, trenches and wrap skirts of Monsieur Saint Laurent’s era to the house classics introduced by Vaccarello, iconic Saint Laurent archetypes are revisited through a contemporary lens. 

Lame, organza, guipure lace, mousseline, brocade, jacquard and metallic cotton amplify the collection’s golden palette, while intricate embroideries and jewelry bring an artisanal dimension to the silhouettes.

As the show draws to a close, gold gives way to black, absorbing the light it once reflected.

description:
Respiro
by Anthony Vaccarello
 
Under the creative direction of Anthony Vaccarello, Saint Laurent unveils Respiro—a campaign photographed by Henrik Purienne that captures the essence of the season through light, movement, and atmosphere.
 
A cinematic ode to summer, Respiro sets in the South of France, from the Mediterranean coastline to Jean Cocteau's Villa Santo Sospir.
 
Through Purienne's instinctive lens, Loli Bahia, SJ, Mona Tougaard, Jenn Du Puy, and Vittoria Ceretti share moments of sunlight, salt water, heat, and shadow creating an effortless sense of intimacy and sensuality.
 
Beyond ready-to-wear and iconic accessories, the campaign extends into the Saint Laurent Rive Droite universe with a curated selection of lifestyle pieces and exclusive collaborations: from the Fieldbar cooler and Tsubota Pearl set to the Wilson tennis racket and Jitensha Electric Tokyo bike, all celebrate an endless summer.

Men’s Summer 2027 
by Anthony Vaccarello
 
Saint Laurent presents the Men’s Summer 2027 collection by Anthony Vaccarello.
 
For Summer 2027, Anthony Vaccarello explores restraint as seduction and the luxury of absence. Rather than excess, the collection considers the power of what remains unsaid, unseen and unknown.
 
Drawing inspiration from figures who embraced reduction as a form of expression, the collection proposes a quiet confidence: where precision replaces spectacle and omission becomes desire.
 
Presented within Fujiko Nakaya’s immersive fog installation, Cloud #07156, models emerge, disappear and reappear through a luminous landscape of mist. Presence and absence become inseparable, extending the collection’s meditation on desire, mystery and restraint.

Tangerine Temptation​
by Anthony Vaccarello​
​
Saint Laurent unveils the Tangerine Temptation campaign, directed by Nadia Lee Cohen.​
​
Featuring Hailey Bieber, alongside Lina Zhang and Jake Hodder, the campaign captures a tension between stillness and expression, disciplined yet magnetic.​
​
Set against the sunlit pools and quiet backyards of Los Angeles, the campaign unfolds with clinical precision. Under the creative direction of Anthony Vaccarello, the Saint Laurent figure is composed, controlled, and unmistakably self-possessed: where attitude is held in posture and distance defines desire.​
​
Swimwear meets relaxed tailoring as structured lines cut through stripped silhouettes. Bold color lingers, while accessories assert their presence with clarity and intent.​
​
The Hortense, Niki, and Amalia bags anchor the series, moving seamlessly through each frame.​

TALKS ​
The Podcast ​
Saint Laurent Rive Droite ​
by Anthony Vaccarello ​

Episode 6 Claire Denis​

Saint Laurent Rive Droite presents Talks, a series of filmed conversations with personalities from cinema, photography, and art, close to Saint Laurent and to Creative Director Anthony Vaccarello. Shot in black and white, the series’ guests are interviewed by French journalist Augustin Trapenard in a minimalist setting, while answering intimate questions about their lives and careers.​

​The sixth episode features French director Claire Denis, who directed The Fence, a film co-produced by Anthony Vaccarello through Saint Laurent Productions.​

During the interview, Claire Denis reflects on memory, power, domination, and the ways in which her work resonates with contemporary tensions. She also discusses her relationship to Africa, the centrality of bodies, desire, and trust in her cinema, and evokes the constraints, fears, and collective commitment that shape her filmmaking.​

Available on Youtube and all major podcast platforms. ​

description:
Women's Winter 26
by Anthony Vaccarello

Saint Laurent presents the Women's Winter 26 by Anthony Vaccarello.

At Saint Laurent, structure is memory. For Winter 2026, the house returns to its most foundational principles: precision, repetition, and the architecture of the body—stripped of nostalgia and distilled to purity.

Tailoring leads. A phalanx of single- and double-breasted black suits sets the rhythm: strong shoulders tapering to a defined waist, silhouettes that move between femininity and masculinity with quiet authority. The collection culminates in a reimagined Le Smoking: nocturnal, insouciant, and resolutely modern.

Cinematic in spirit, the collection draws on the restrained intensity of Romy Schneider in Max et les Ferrailleurs and the emotional depth of Tennessee Williams’ heroines in The Roman Spring of Mrs. Stone. Bourgeois stillness meets urban vulnerability; fragility becomes force, structure becomes seduction.

Each look affirms clothing as intimacy and intention: precision over spectacle, emotion over excess.

Episode 5 Jim Jarmusch ​
​
Saint Laurent Rive Droite presents Talks, a new series of filmed conversations with personalities from cinema, photography, and art, close to Saint Laurent and to Creative Director Anthony Vaccarello. Shot in black and white, the series’ guests are interviewed by French journalist Augustin Trapenard in a minimalist setting, while answering intimate questions about their lives and careers. ​
​
The fifth episode features American director and musician Jim Jarmusch, who directed Father Mother Brother Sister, a film co-produced by Anthony Vaccarello through Saint Laurent Productions.​
​
During the interview, Jarmusch talks about his obsession for Japanese cinema and how an entire story relies in the eyes, the gesture and the movement of its actors. ​
​

Blurry Moon, co-produced by Saint Laurent and Because Music, directed by Anthony Vaccarello, written and performed by Charlotte Gainsbourg, produced and arranged by SebastiAn.
 
The music video marks Vaccarello’s directorial debut. 
 
With Blurry Moon, Vaccarello pursues his dialogue between disciplines adding music into Saint Laurent’s cultural vision—following its pioneering steps into cinema.
 
In Los Angeles, on the legendary Mulholland Drive, Anthony Vaccarello unveils a new facet of his creative universe.
 
For Saint Laurent, he directs Charlotte Gainsbourg and creates an atmosphere both intimate and cinematic, inspired by Lynch and Angelo Badalamenti—an offbeat tribute to Hollywood’s daydreams and illusions.
 
At the wheel, Charlotte lets her thoughts drift. Little by little, the car drives itself, guided by an invisible force—a subtle metaphor for absence and memory. Vaccarello transforms this simple ride into a cinematic moment.
 
This extended sequence captures raw emotion, where Saint Laurent elegance merges with the luminous melancholy of the Hollywood Hills.

Men's Summer 26
by Anthony Vaccarello

For the Summer 2026 menswear show, Anthony Vaccarello evokes a suspended moment, somewhere between Paris and Fire Island, where escape became elegance, and desire became a language.

This collection pays tribute to a lost generation, to the artists — Stanton, Angus, Ellis — who gave a face to silent desires.
And to Yves Saint Laurent, of course, who in 1974 sought refuge, only to create anew.

Inspired by a time when desire was style,
when beauty served as a shield against emptiness,
the collection explores this subtle sensuality, that fragile moment when one dresses as much to reveal oneself as to hide.

Ambiguity becomes elegance.

For this collection, Anthony Vaccarello chooses not the night, but the clarity of the afternoon light.
A deliberate rupture.
No artificial glow.
Just dry light. Full presence.
A geometry of exposure.
Not to display — but to hold.

The palette is hushed — sand, salt, pale ochre, dry moss, pool blue.

Nothing is declarative.
Everything is held.
A sensuality without theatre.

During the interview, Cronenberg talks about the film The Shrouds, which reflects his personal life, almost as an autobiography evoking the disappearance of his wife. description:
Anthony Vaccarello presents the Saint Laurent Women's Winter 25 Collection

From the beginning, a simplicity of silhouette, as if created with a few pencil strokes, has defined the Saint Laurent ideal. 

With straightforward pieces free of superfluous details, Anthony Vaccarello’s Winter 2025 Women’s collection affirms this founding ethos. Instead of speaking through ornament or padding, fabrics and precise construction shape the garments. Pure forms and volumes are derived from construction and cut. 

Ample stone-washed skirts worn with leather blousons create ambiguity, while a concise palette, saturated versions of signature Saint Laurent colors, fills out the collection’s clear lines. 

To achieve a novel, more technical texture, stretch fabrics are paired with guipure, couture fabrics are distressed, and cigaline silk printed with iconic animal and floral motifs is submerged in silicone. 

As a counterweight to the clothes' minimalism, pointed shoes are embellished with a satin square rose. Accessorizing jewelry is made of rock crystal, a lucky stone favored by Yves Saint Laurent. 

The set, a grand onyx oval, reflects the collection’s otherworldly mineral feel, as glowing walls suggest both impenetrability and unmined depth, their rich patterns a snapshot of human complexity.

description:
Anthony Vaccarello presents the Saint Laurent Men’s Winter 25 Collection.

A productive tension between temperamental opposites has been a hallmark of Saint Laurent since the house’s foundingby a pair of distinct personalities – an aesthete hungry for new experiences and a steady literary mastermind. 

For Saint Laurent Winter 2025 menswear, creative director Anthony Vaccarello highlights this innate duality.Contrast defines the collection, as counterintuitive elements inject surprising fluidity into concise tailoring. Inspired by the classicwardrobe introduced by Yves Saint Laurent in his Haute Couture or Rive Gauche collections and by the spirit of Robert Mapplethorpe, a menacing, seductive elegance informs both the silhouette as well as individual pieces. Throughout, unexpectedpairings render the brand’s signature ambiguity novel, evident in the way ample feather-trimmed coats and sharp double-breastedjackets shift in character once intrepidly accessorised with high wader-like leather boots.

The prevailing polarity – between somber and light, soft and firm, voluminous and tapered – extends to the set: for the occasion,the minimalist lines and cool surfaces of the Bourse de Commerce are juxtaposed with rich, weathered parquet flooringthat evokes the opulent salons of the past, as do enormous crystal chandeliers – a nod to the Intercontinental Hotel’s ballroom,where the house presented its Haute Couture collections between 1975 and 2001.

description:
Women's Summer 25 Show 
by Anthony Vaccarello

No other house is as linked to a quintessential female archetype as Saint Laurent, whose ideal woman is more complex than the seductive perfection of classic muses. As Yves Saint Laurent could have said, I am the Saint Laurent woman. The Saint Laurent woman loves to indulge in darker penchants, an attraction to danger and pleasure she proudly owns in her modern agency.
Anthony Vaccarello develops what has set the House apart from day one: the relevance of Saint Laurent clothes is distilled from the independent attitude of the woman who wears them. Her contradictions reflect Yves Saint Laurent’s own persona, in which artful sophistication coexisted with instinctual desire.
 
To illustrate this, part of the collection recalls Yves Saint Laurent’s way of dressing, with fluid suits and jackets over blazers. A different side of the same character emerges in a more opulent skirt-dominated section. These ensembles echo the vibrant garments often seen in the works of painters the house founder cherished. 
 
Over the years, the Saint Laurent woman's multi-faceted allure has been embodied most eloquently by a special group of models with whom the house has forged lasting relationships. Selected both for their diverse singularity and for the way they symbolize a novel feminine ideal, these personalities are integral to the Saint Laurent universe. In an homage, tonight all looks are named after women that have been important to the house at

description:
Saint Laurent Rive Droite, through SL Editions, is pleased to present a new book, featuring Zoë Kravitz photographed by Henrik Purienne.

Titled ZOË, the book reflects the longstanding relationship between the actress and Saint Laurent creativedirector Anthony Vaccarello. In real life, as in her work, Kravitz personifies the confident, contemporarysensuality that is the essence of the Saint Laurent woman. The pair’s respectful vision is distilled in ZOË.On over 100 pages, the shots captured by Purienne’s lens in color and black-and-white show Kravitz'scharacter —independent, playful, and in clear command of her allure— in a variety of situations unfolding fromthe beach to the city. A small cast of supporting players —including actor Jeremy Allen White— adds intrigueto the simultaneously abstract and revealing story.

With the publication’s release, Saint Laurent continues to explore creative collaborations that advancethe cinematic scope of Vaccarello’s direction for the house. ZOË will be available at Saint Laurent Babylone, Paris, and at Saint Laurent Rive Droite in Los Angeles as well as on YSL.COM. To markthe occasion, images from the book will be exhibited concurrently at both locations.

description:
Saint Laurent Productions presents the trailer for "Parthenope" directed by Paolo Sorrentino.

The movie was in competition at the 77th Cannes Film Festival and stars Dario Aita, Celeste Dalla Porta, Silvia Degrandi, Isabella Ferrari, Lorenzo Gleijeses, Biagio Izzo, Marlon Joubert, Peppe Lanzetta, Nella Mascia, Gary Oldman, Silvio Orlando, Luisa Ranieri, Daniele Rienzo, Stefania Sandrelli & Alfonso Santagata. 

The long journey of Parthenope's life, from her birth in 1950 till today. A feminine epic, devoid of heroism but brimming with an inexorable passion for freedom, Naples, and the faces of love-all those true, pointless, and unspeakable loves. The perfect Capri summer, the lightheartedness of youth. Which ends in ambush. And then all the others-the Neapolitans, men and women, observed and loved, disillusioned and vital, their waves of melancholy, their tragic ironies and dejected glances. Life, be it ordinary or memorable, knows how to be very long. The passing of time offers up a vast repertoire of emotions. And there in the background, so close and so very far, is Naples, this ineffable city that bewitches, enchants, screams, laughs, and always knows how to hurt you. 

Production: Fremantle, The Apartment Pictures, a Fremantle Company, Saint Laurent by Anthony Vaccarello, Pathé, Numero 10, A24, Piper Film

When the Sky Blooms with Sakura

Commissioned by Anthony Vaccarello for Saint Laurent, the artist Cai Guo-Qiang created daytime fireworks titled When the Sky Blooms with Sakura, at Yotsukura Beach in Iwaki City, an area that had been devastated by the 2011 Japan earthquake and the resulting tsunami. 
The instant bloom of the sakura in the sky conveys collective hope and a future where one day the land can become a pink sea of sakura.

description:
French Modernists
Exhibition curated
by Anthony Vaccarello
at Saint Laurent Rive Droite 

Anthony Vaccarello has curated an exhibition dedicated to French Modernist design with a selection of vintage furniture. Mainly featuring the works of Jean-Michel Frank, it also highlights some designs by Jacques Adnet and Jean Després.

Jean-Michel Frank’s radical minimal touch decorated the homes of the intellectual and artistic elite pre-war, and although forgotten about after the war, he was rediscovered in the 1960s to great acclaim. His works, now almost a century old, mixed luxury and rare materials with new ones to create pieces of functionality, beauty, and elegance. 

Another great figure of French Modernism, designer Jacques Adnet constructed strong pieces often devoid of any decoration, integrating glass, ceramics, and metal to add charisma.

Finally, Jean Després’s innovative works illustrated the elegance and inventive spirit of the roaring twenties.

VENICE INTERNATIONAL FILM FESTIVAL 2020

Sportin’ Life is the sixth incarnation of the international art project, SELF - curated by Saint Laurent’s creative director, Anthony Vaccarello.

The documentary is an exploration into the sources and personal history of creativity, the essential life of an artist. Raw and sharp – it has the feeling of a moment in time that is still happening.
Abel Ferrara’s intimate and lush look at his own life, his world refracted through his art - music, filmmaking, his collaborators and inspirations such as Ferrara’s early works and his creative partnerships with Willem Dafoe, Joe Delia, Paul Hipp and the musicians who inspired this work.

CURATED by WONG KAR WAI
PRESENTED by ANTHONY VACCARELLO
DIRECTED by WING SHYA 

”A night in Shanghai” is a story about the introspective research of our-self, which starts from breaking the balance. Ju Xiaowen is walking on the wire, trying to find the balance in real life by comparing the past and the present, sharply contrasting. Looking for who she is and moved by the desire to express herself.

Saint Laurent SELF 05, “A night in Shanghai”, marks the fifth chapter of the project, following Daido Moriyama, Vanessa Beecroft, Bret Easton Ellis and Gaspar Noé.

description:
SAINT LAURENT - SELF 04 - LUX ÆTERNA 
BY ANTHONY VACCARELLO 
FILMED BY GASPAR NOE 

Cannes Film Festival selected “Lux Æterna”, a 50 minute “film within the film” directed by Gaspar Noé, in Official Selection, as part of the midnight session projected on the 18th of May at Théâtre Lumière. 

A vibrant essay on respect for beliefs, the actor’s craft and the art of filmmaking that stages Béatrice Dalle, Charlotte Gainsbourg, Abbey Lee, Anatole Devoucoux du Buysson, Clara 3000, Claude-Emmanuelle Gajan-Maull, Felix Maritaud, Fred Cambier, Karl Glusman, Lola Pillu Perier, Loup “Vuk” Brankovic, Luka Isaac, Maxime Ruiz, Mica Arganaraz, Paul Hameline, Philippe Mensah, Stefania Cristian, Tom Kan, Victor Sekularac and Yannick Bono.
 
Featuring Béatrice Dalle and Charlotte Gainsbourg.

“Lux Æterna” marks the fourth chapter of the project, following Daido Moriyama, Vanessa Beecroft and Bret Easton Ellis.

title: SAINT LAURENT - WOMEN SUMMER 2019

description:
SAINT LAURENT - SELF 02 
ART INSTALLATION - VANESSA BEECROFT
BY ANTHONY VACCARELLO 
MIAMI ART BASEL - DECEMBER 1-15, 2018 

From self, personality, to Saint Laurent.

The intention of the project is to capture different aspects of the Saint Laurent personality, underlining the complexity of various individuals through the eyes of artists selected by Anthony Vaccarello. It represents the freedom of self-expression without censorship, and conveys many differ ent facets of the Saint Laurent attitude. 

Creative disciplines across art and fashion reinforce and fuel the concept of diversity, individuality, and self-confidence through a lens free from pretense and hypocrisy. This project is an artistic commentary on society while emphasizing the core values of Saint Laurent. Self is formed by a heady mixture of attraction, ambivalence and mystery generated by photographers, artists, and filmmakers who have come together to make a confrontational statement.

This installation marks the second chapter of the project, following Daido Moriyama.

More on SELF: https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLE05euBYOyJrOQ0poA9mRWodq2LYxucXP
